# Liferay Design, repository guide for LLMs

Project: liferay-design/design.liferay.com
Repo: https://github.com/liferay-design/design.liferay.com
Site: https://design.liferay.com
Purpose: Public website for Liferay Design. Content-driven Gatsby site with articles, Lexicon design system docs, events, and team pages.

Note: the canonical, more detailed guide is CLAUDE.md at the repo root. Keep this file in sync with it.

## Critical compatibility constraints
- Node 18.x (18.20.8, pinned in .nvmrc). Gatsby 5 needs Node >= 18. Run `nvm use` inside the repo.
- Gatsby 5.16, React 18.3, MDX v2. Do not assume Gatsby 2/3/4, React 16, or MDX v1 patterns.
- MDX v2: templates render page content with `{children}`; the `MDXRenderer`/`body` field no longer exists. HTML comments are invalid in MDX, stray `<` must be escaped, and `style` must be an object.
- YAML/JSON data `id` is exposed as `yamlId`/`jsonId` (Gatsby 4+).
- GraphQL sort uses the Gatsby 5 shape: `sort: { field: DESC }`.
- `timeToRead` is a custom resolver in gatsby-node.js (Gatsby 5 dropped the built-in field).
- theme-ui 0.17: use `Themed` from `@theme-ui/mdx`, `ThemeUIProvider`, and `@emotion/react`.
- sass (dart-sass) ~1.32 is pinned so node-sass-era SCSS keeps compiling without warnings.
- CSS modules use default exports (`import styles from '*.module.scss'`), preserved via `cssLoaderOptions` in gatsby-plugin-sass.
- .npmrc sets `legacy-peer-deps=true`; keep it for local installs and Netlify.
- Stability over modernization. Do not upgrade Gatsby, React, Node, or sass as part of a small task.

## Start-up and local development
- `nvm use`, then `npm install`, then `npm run dev`.
- Dev server runs on http://0.0.0.0:7777.
- src/utils/generateEnv.js auto-creates a placeholder .env.development if it is missing.
- Some sections need API keys (Google APIs, Firebase). The site degrades gracefully without them; do not remove code that looks odd if it protects no-key builds.

## Deployment
- Netlify, pinned to Node 18 via netlify.toml (`NODE_VERSION = "18"`).
- Redirect rules live in static/_redirects. Keep only rules that point at Liferay-controlled hosts.

## Live vs deprecated scope
- The build only includes the core sections: Home, Articles, Events, Team, Alumni, Lexicon, plus Tags and Changelog.
- Everything else (handbook, blueprints, resources, careers, newsletter, yearly reports 2018-2021, office-hours, design-week, lexicon-1) is parked under deprecated/ and does not build. Gatsby only sources ./src.
- One exception: /resources/license is still live, served by src/pages/resources/license.js.
- Before adding content or fixing a page, confirm it belongs to a live section.

## High-level structure
- src/markdown: site content for the live sections, plus YAML data (Authors, Changelog, Countries, Offices).
- src/components: atomic design (atoms, molecules, organisms, templates).
- src/pages: page entry points (home, articles, team, alumni, lexicon, events, tags, changelog). Every .js under src/pages becomes a page, including colocated components/ files.
- src/utils: helpers (generateEnv, generateIcons, typography, logRocket).
- static: public assets (images, icons, files, videos, admin, _redirects).
- deprecated: outdated sections kept out of the build. Restore by moving a folder back under src/.

## Routing and page generation
- MDX/Markdown files in src/markdown/{section}/ get slugs via createFilePath() with /markdown/ stripped.
- The first slug segment maps to a template: /articles/... -> src/components/templates/Articles/index.js.
- Pages are created with `component: \`${template}?__contentFilePath=${node.internal.contentFilePath}\``.
- Tag pages are generated at /tags/<kebab-case-tag>/.

## Content model
- Editorial work happens under src/markdown; do not move content from markdown into React components.
- Content changes: check src/markdown first, then the YAML data files, and only then React components if content is hardcoded.
- New MDX content should match an existing template slug unless you are intentionally adding a new template and updating gatsby-node.js and navigation.

## Styling and theming
- Mixed model; check the local area before changing it.
- gatsby-browser.js imports theme/global.scss.
- SCSS modules (.module.scss) per component.
- Theme UI config in src/gatsby-plugin-theme-ui.
- Typography in src/utils/typography.js.

## Icons and assets
- SVGs in static/images/icons are turned into a React map by `npm run icons`, written to src/components/atoms/Icon/icons.js.
- Do not hand-edit the generated icon file.

## Guidance for AI assistants
- Read CLAUDE.md first; it is the source of truth for constraints and workflow.
- Prefer content changes in src/markdown and small component fixes over architectural refactors.
- Check whether a page is driven by MDX + template before editing a page component directly.
- Do not apply Gatsby 2/3/4, React 16, or MDX v1 patterns.
- Do not commit secrets, API keys, or OAuth client credentials. Use .env.development locally and Netlify environment variables in production.
